acceptance.given: The validator evaluates the three named evaluation seed occurrences in the toolchain seed manifest.

oracle.expected: Each occurrence is represented exactly once and has an explicit applicability field recorded alongside provenance, missing-label, counterexample-or-explicit-absence, and approved non-baseline classification; validation passes only when all three applicability records are present.
forbidden: Any named seed occurrence lacks applicability.
Applicability is inferred from another occurrence or omitted from the occurrence record.
oracle.observable: The evaluated seed manifest and validator result show three distinct occurrence records, each with a non-empty applicability value and a passing applicability assertion.

acceptance.then: The validator records applicability for every named evaluation seed occurrence.
acceptance.when: During evaluation of the named seed manifest.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a seed manifest fixture in which one of the three named occurrences omits applicability; validation must fail with the missing occurrence identified.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate and persist explicit applicability on each named evaluation seed occurrence while preserving exactly-once occurrence and provenance requirements.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing seed-manifest fields and accept only additive applicability metadata; invalid or missing applicability remains rejected.

slice_hint.state_transition: Seed occurrence without applicability becomes a validator failure; three complete occurrences pass applicability validation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator passes only when all three named seed occurrence records each contain explicit applicability and the complete FR-6 record set.

acceptance.given: A replay result is produced by the toolchain replay worker.

oracle.expected: The result contains a binding to a complete Current Snapshot whose required contents are all present, and the binding identity is recorded with the result.
forbidden: A replay result is unbound from its Current Snapshot.
The bound snapshot is incomplete or partial.
A result is treated as valid solely because a snapshot path exists.
oracle.observable: The replay result artifact includes a current-snapshot identity and complete content manifest, and the replay contract test verifies the association before accepting the result.

acceptance.then: The replay result is associated with a complete Current Snapshot.
acceptance.when: When a replay result is produced and validated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a replay-result fixture whose current snapshot manifest omits a required file or binding identity; the replay validator must reject the result as incomplete.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require every replay result to carry and validate a complete Current Snapshot identity and content manifest before success is emitted.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing replay result fields backward-compatible; missing snapshot identity or required content fails closed rather than being synthesized.

slice_hint.state_transition: An unbound or incomplete replay result is rejected or stale; a complete Current Snapshot binding is eligible for subsequent replay evaluation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: No replay result is accepted unless its recorded Current Snapshot identity resolves to a complete required-content manifest and the association is verified by the replay contract test.

acceptance.given: Validator evaluation compares the candidate package against the toolchain external-trust policy and independent trust evidence.

oracle.expected: An independent candidate-external-trust check executes and records evidence tied to the candidate identity; validation passes only when that check succeeds independently.
forbidden: Candidate-external trust is inferred solely from another verification result.
Trust evidence is bound to a different candidate identity.
oracle.observable: The validator output contains a dedicated candidate-external-trust assertion and evidence record whose candidate identity matches the evaluated package.

acceptance.when: During validator evaluation of a candidate package.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a validator result containing source, content, and compatibility checks but no dedicated candidate-external-trust assertion; validation must fail for omitted independent trust verification.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add an independently evaluated candidate-external-trust assertion bound to the candidate identity and prevent other checks from satisfying it transitively.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing candidate identity and trust-policy interfaces; missing independent trust evidence fails closed.

slice_hint.state_transition: A candidate package without independent external-trust evidence fails validation; matching independent evidence passes the trust assertion.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator cannot emit success unless a dedicated candidate-external-trust check passes for the same candidate identity and is independently observable in the result.

acceptance.given: The validator evaluates an adversarial dependency case in the toolchain semantic gate.

oracle.expected: The adversarial dependency case receives a non-success verdict and the result records the dependency violation as the determining reason.
forbidden: Success is accepted for an adversarial dependency case.
A reused or unrelated evidence record is used to mark the case successful.
The dependency violation is ignored or downgraded to an informational warning.
oracle.observable: The semantic-gate result for the selected adversarial dependency case contains a deterministic non-success verdict with a dependency-specific failure code or assertion.

acceptance.then: The adversarial dependency case is rejected as non-success.
acceptance.when: When an adversarial dependency case is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the adversarial dependency fixture that would otherwise yield success; execute the semantic gate and require a non-success verdict identifying the dependency violation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure adversarial dependency violations deterministically reject success and remain visible as the result-determining failure.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep ordinary dependency evaluation behavior unchanged; only adversarial dependency violations force non-success and fail closed.

slice_hint.state_transition: An adversarial dependency case produces a dependency-specific non-success verdict; a clean dependency case follows the existing success path.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: For the selected adversarial dependency case, the semantic gate emits a non-success verdict whose determining evidence identifies the dependency violation; any success verdict fails the check.
